bull_bear.body: Fuel/laminate inflation persistence; delayed normalization of dual pricing in B2B channels; El Nino impact on milk supply; geopolitical disruption in Middle East; e-commerce channel conflict if INR 5/10 packs are pushed
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, proactive, and execution-focused; emphasized agility, CEP discipline, and long-term brand building; acknowledged short-term headwinds but projected normalization by Q1FY27
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: E-commerce contribution is 12%+ when excluding low-price biscuits (not 6%); 70% of e-commerce sales now via quick commerce enabling premiumization; women manage majority of factories; INR 5/10 packs are deliberately deprioritized on e-commerce to avoid channel conflict; tax reversal (INR 200cr) boosted PAT by ~800bps
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Century-long brand franchise - the Board presented the 107th Annual Report of the Company, and the Corporate Governance Report describes 'a legacy spanning over a century'
- Extensive sales and distribution network, strengthened during the year through improved outlet servicing, enhanced rural reach and focused interventions across key geographies
- Rural reach architecture built on Rural Preferred Dealers, last-mile distribution and value-led pack-price formats at the ` 5/- and ` 10/- price points that dominate volumes
- Manufacturing scale and locational advantage - 20 state-of-the-art factories with integrated warehousing and distribution, enabling freshness and short lead times
- Innovation and premiumisation engine across biscuit, cake, dairy and adjacent categories, including India's 1st DHA-enriched biscuit 'Milk Bikis SMART' with 16 micronutrients
- Structural cost-efficiency programs across the value chain (manufacturing productivity, energy efficiency, packaging optimisation, freight and distribution rationalisation) that protect margins in a volatile cost environment
- International footprint across more than 80 countries operating largely through a national distributor-led model spanning the Middle East, Americas, Africa, Europe and Asia Pacific
- Omnichannel route-to-market spanning traditional trade for mass and rural consumption alongside Modern Trade, E-commerce and Quick commerce for premium and impulse-led purchases
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input cost volatility across key agri and energy commodities — Management calls out volatility in the cost of key input items such as wheat, sugar, milk, edible oils, crude oil & gas as a key risk that may require calibrated pricing and cost management actions; elevated cocoa costs are separately flagged as pressuring Cake category profitability. Because the portfolio is commodity-intensive and price-sensitive at the ` 5/- and ` 10/- points, cost spikes cannot be fully passed through without hurting volumes.
- Competitive intensity from regional, unorganised and digitally native players — Competition from regional and unorganised players in value segments and emerging brands in premium segments may continue to exert pressure on pricing, profitability and market share. In Cake, low entry barriers keep the category highly fragmented; in Bread, insurgent and niche brands are investing in innovation and premium positioning; in Rusk, pricing is the key competitive differentiator in a commoditised structure.
- Shifting consumer preferences towards health, nutrition and clean-label products — Evolving preferences necessitate continuous portfolio adaptation and innovation; management notes that preference for healthier alternatives may affect demand for traditional offerings, requiring continuous portfolio innovation and renovation to stay relevant.
- Execution complexity from the shift to Digital and Quick commerce channels — Increasing reliance on Digital and Quick commerce adds execution complexity in demand planning, inventory management and channel economics, even as these channels grow faster than traditional trade and drive discovery and premiumisation.
- Geopolitical exposure and currency volatility in international markets — The International Business remains exposed to geopolitical developments in the Middle East and currency volatility in parts of Africa and the Levant region, leading to rising input and freight costs that may impact growth and profitability.
- Modern Trade dominance raising the cost of operations overseas — Modern Trade dominance in several international markets increases the cost of operations, while competition from both local and global players necessitates continued agility and focused execution.
- Dairy-specific margin exposure - milk procurement cost, seasonality and value-added competition — The Dairy business remains exposed to volatility in milk procurement costs which may impact margins and profitability; the value-added dairy segment faces heightened competition from organised and regional players, and demand in certain dairy categories is influenced by seasonal consumption patterns.
- Category-development risk in early-stage and occasion-dependent categories — Croissant remains at an early stage of development with relatively low consumer awareness, requiring sustained investment in category creation, consumer education and distribution to unlock growth; Rusk stays closely tied to tea-consumption occasions, making it important to broaden consumer appeal and expand usage occasions. The Company's cautionary statement additionally lists raw material availability and/or prices, cyclical demand, pricing, competitive actions, disruptions due to pandemic and/or natural calamities and changes in government and/or tax regulations as factors that could make a difference to operations.

business.body:

business.body: Britannia manufactures and sells branded packaged food, reporting performance as one segment i.e., 'Foods'. Its bakery business covers biscuits, cakes, rusk and bread; its dairy business spans value-added categories; and its adjacent business covers newer snacking formats such as wafers and croissants. The Company sells to urban and rural Indian consumers across traditional trade, Modern Trade, E-commerce and Quick commerce, and runs an International Business across more than 80 countries largely through a national distributor-led model.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Dairy: strengthen the value-added portfolio, leverage integrated dairy infrastructure and expand consumer reach across channels while maintaining focus on quality, operational efficiency and sustainable sourcing
- Dairy: improve capacity utilisation across all manufacturing lines at the dairy facility to support portfolio expansion and cater to growing demand for value-added dairy categories
- Dairy: targeted innovation in nutrition-focused and differentiated products - 'Britannia The Laughing Cow Daily Cheese Slices' made from 100% cow milk and entry into the high-protein segment with 'Come Alive Greek Yogurt' (Classic, Blueberry, Strawberry)
- Dairy: backward integration into milk procurement centred on breeding, feeding and livestock management, supported by farmer training programmes, animal health camps, deworming drives and cattle feed distribution
- Channel strategy: strengthen availability across retail outlets and drive localised demand generation, while directing Modern Trade and E-commerce investments towards competitiveness and visibility
- Wafer: strengthen presence in priority markets, expand participation in high-growth formats such as wafer rolls (reimagining Bourbon as 'Bourbon Rolls') and deepen consumer engagement, including a first-of-its-kind Naruto anime collaboration with QR-enabled on-pack activations
- Croissant: invest in product innovation and premium positioning, complemented by competitive pricing interventions, to build the packaged Croissant category in India and hold leadership in it
- International: strengthen brand equity and consumer affinity among the Indian diaspora through brand-building, visibility and promotional initiatives
- International: expand the portfolio through innovation - 'Britannia Chompers Mini Chocochip Cookies', 'Chompers Mini Rainbow Cookies', 'Milk Bikis Minis Wafflez', 'Milk Bikis Minis Kreemz' and 'Pure Magic' Italian Custard and Peanut Creme Filled Choco Biscuits
- International: customise distribution across MENA, Americas and Asia Pacific with increased focus on mainstream retail and E-commerce, plus entry into white-space markets to capture untapped demand
- International: evaluate expansion of operations in emerging markets through contract manufacturing, partnerships and other strategic avenues
- International: drive profitability through calibrated pricing actions and cost-efficiency initiatives including automation, recipe and packaging optimisation, logistics efficiencies and sourcing optimisation
- Portfolio-wide: strengthen the brand portfolio, drive innovation, enhance distribution effectiveness, improve supply chain agility, expand presence across emerging channels and maintain disciplined cost management
- Sustainability is integrated into operations through renewable energy adoption, resource efficiency, responsible sourcing, packaging optimisation and community development programs, aligning environmental responsibility with operational efficiency and long-term cost sustainability
- Adoption of alternative fuel used during the year as a mitigation measure alongside prudent inventory management and hedging
- Structural cost efficiency programs covering increased manufacturing productivity & energy efficiency and optimised packaging
- Expansion of the 'better-for-you' portfolio through nutrition-led, millet-based and other healthier offerings, providing more wholesome and fibre-rich options across categories
- Reasonable Assurance obtained on BRSR Core - a set of KPIs/metrics under 9 Environmental, Social and Governance attributes - from TUV SUD South Asia Private Limited, with BRSR disclosures made on a consolidated basis
- Women represent 9.09% of the Board of Directors and 33.33% of Key Management Personnel as on 31 March 2026; women are 44.74% of total workers and 12.69% of total employees
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for every NGRBC stakeholder group - communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners - with complaint counts and pending resolution disclosed for FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
- Business activity is 100% FMCG - manufacturing, trading and selling of food products - with Bakery Products and Salted Snacks at ~97% of turnover and Dairy Products at ~3%; International Business contributes ~6% of consolidated turnover
- Independent Auditor's Certificate confirms the Company complied, in all material respects, with the conditions of corporate governance stipulated in the SEBI Listing Regulations for the year ended 31 March 2026
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Britannia's expansion in FY 2025-26 was largely about deepening existing assets rather than building new ones. The manufacturing and supply chain network comprises 20 state-of-the-art factories supported by an integrated warehousing and distribution infrastructure, strategically located to minimise lead times and preserve product freshness; during the year the Company focused on optimising existing capacities rather than adding greenfield capacity. In Dairy, the state-of-the-art facility at Ranjangaon, Maharashtra, with a milk processing capacity of ~5 lakh litres per day, continues to anchor the multi-category dairy strategy, manufacturing Cheese, Flavoured Milk, Skimmed Milk Powder, Butter, Ghee, Dairy Whitener, Greek Yogurt and Curd; the year's focus was on improving capacity utilisation across all manufacturing lines to support portfolio expansion into value-added dairy. Backward integration continued on the input side, with over 60,000 litres of milk per day procured through a network of over 2,500 farmers, supported by breeding, feeding and livestock management programmes, farmer training, animal health camps, deworming drives and cattle feed distribution. Category expansion is being pursued through distribution rather than plant capex - targeted distribution expansion for differentiated rusk variants (Milk Rusk, Butter Rusk, Cake Rusk alongside the core Premium Bake Rusk portfolio), Quick commerce platform partnerships in Bread, and expanded availability across geographies. Internationally, the Company continues to evaluate opportunities to expand operations in emerging markets through contract manufacturing, partnerships and other strategic avenues, customising distribution across MENA, Americas and Asia Pacific and entering white-space markets, while pursuing automation, recipe and packaging optimisation, logistics efficiencies and sourcing optimisation. The Board's Report records no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report, and no change in the nature of the Company's business during the year. No rupee capex figure or dated commissioning schedule for a new project is disclosed in the routed sections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian economy expected to sustain strong growth momentum relative to global peers, with real GDP growth projected in the range of ~6.5 to 7%, supported by resilient domestic demand, stable financial systems and continued policy support
- Inflation expected to remain broadly within the RBI's target range, though geopolitical developments in energy markets and global supply chains may continue to influence input costs and demand conditions
- Categories supported by favourable demographic trends, increasing urbanisation, rising disposable incomes and growing preference for branded and convenient food products
- Biscuit: demand supported by favourable demographics, urbanisation, nuclear households and on-the-go lifestyles; premiumisation in urban markets and growing rural penetration provide both volume and value growth avenues
- Cake: growth potential from increasing household penetration, product innovation and premiumisation across differentiated formats such as Donuts and Brownies
- Rusk: fragmented, predominantly unorganised market structure creates an opportunity for organised players with strong brands, extensive distribution and consistent quality
- Bread: rising demand for protein-rich, high-fibre, clean-label and differentiated variants provides avenues for innovation and premiumisation, with Quick commerce enhancing access and visibility
- Dairy: adoption of Quick commerce and E-commerce is expanding consumer access, while health, wellness and convenience preferences support high-protein, nutrition-focused and ready-to-consume dairy
- Wafer: low category penetration plus growing traction in premium wafer rolls supports consumer expansion, product discovery and category development
- Croissant: increasing consumer acceptance of global bakery formats, rising disposable incomes and preference for indulgent, premium snacking as awareness expands beyond early adopters and Gen Z cohorts
- International: positioned for growth across GCC countries, Americas and Africa supported by E-commerce expansion, localised manufacturing and portfolios tailored to regional preferences, with white-space potential in Latin America, Asia, Europe and Russia
- Margin levers: calibrated pricing actions plus cost-efficiency initiatives - automation, recipe and packaging optimisation, logistics efficiencies and sourcing optimisation
- Watch-items on the demand/cost side: volatility in wheat, sugar, edible oils, crude oil & gas and cocoa; milk procurement cost volatility in Dairy; competitive intensity from regional/unorganised players in value segments and digitally native brands in premium segments
- Execution complexity is rising with increasing reliance on Digital and Quick commerce channels, in areas such as demand planning, inventory management and channel economics
- International cost headwinds from Middle East geopolitics, currency volatility in parts of Africa and the Levant, and Modern Trade dominance raising the cost of operations
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Britannia delivered strong 7.5% revenue and 16.3% PAT growth in FY26 despite West Asia logistics disruption and dual pricing in rural wholesale channels; margin resilience was maintained through CEP efficiency, strategic price hikes, and e-commerce premiumization, with FY27 outlook supported by normalized trade channels and accelerated D2C growth.

open.item: The Board recommended a Final Dividend of ` 90.50/- per Equity Share of face value of ` 1/- each for FY 2025-26 for approval of Members at the 107th AGM, payable to Members on the record date of Friday, 31 July 2026.

A Final Dividend of ` 90.50/- per Equity Share of face value of ` 1/- each for the financial year ended 31 March 2026 is proposed for declaration at the 107th AGM, payable to Members on the record date of Friday, 31 July 2026.

M/s. GNV & Associates, Cost and Management Accountants, have been re-appointed by the Board as Cost Auditors to conduct the audit of the Cost Records of the Company for the financial year ending 31 March 2027, with remuneration placed for ratification at the 107th AGM.

Britannia will expand rural reach through scaling up Rural Preferred Dealers, strengthening last-mile distribution and enhancing product availability across key consumption areas, supported by calibrated pack-price interventions and value-led formats.
Britannia will continue to invest in brand building, innovation and supply chain efficiencies to reinforce its leadership position and drive sustainable growth across the Biscuit category.

Britannia continues to implement structural cost efficiency programs across the value chain covering manufacturing productivity, energy efficiency, packaging optimisation and freight & distribution rationalisation to protect margins in a volatile cost environment.

Management flagged that geopolitical tensions, especially in the Middle East, caused temporary supply chain disruptions and logistics challenges, with higher freight and shipping costs adversely impacting profitability of the International Business.
Britannia is focused on improving capacity utilisation across all its dairy manufacturing lines to support portfolio expansion and cater to growing demand for value-added dairy categories.
Britannia continues to evaluate opportunities to expand its operations in emerging markets through contract manufacturing, partnerships and other strategic avenues.

The International Business will increase focus on mainstream retail and E-commerce platforms across MENA, Americas and Asia Pacific, alongside entry into white-space markets to capture untapped demand.

The International Business will pursue calibrated pricing actions and multiple cost-efficiency initiatives - automation, recipe and packaging optimisation, logistics efficiencies and sourcing optimisation - to improve profitability.

Through sustained investment in product innovation, category creation and consumer engagement, Britannia intends to strengthen its leadership position and drive development of the packaged Croissant category in India.
Management flagged volatility in the cost of key inputs such as wheat, sugar, milk, edible oils, crude oil & gas as a key risk that may require calibrated pricing and cost management actions.
Management flagged that increasing reliance on Digital and Quick commerce channels adds execution complexity in demand planning, inventory management and channel economics.

Portfolio strengthening in Rusk remains a key strategic priority along with expanding the reach of differentiated variants such as Milk Rusk, Butter Rusk and Cake Rusk beside the core Premium Bake Rusk portfolio, supported by targeted distribution expansion.

currentContext.expansion: Britannia's expansion in FY 2025-26 was largely about deepening existing assets rather than building new ones. The manufacturing and supply chain network comprises 20 state-of-the-art factories supported by an integrated warehousing and distribution infrastructure, strategically located to minimise lead times and preserve product freshness; during the year the Company focused on optimising existing capacities rather than adding greenfield capacity. In Dairy, the state-of-the-art facility at Ranjangaon, Maharashtra, with a milk processing capacity of ~5 lakh litres per day, continues to anchor the multi-category dairy strategy, manufacturing Cheese, Flavoured Milk, Skimmed Milk Powder, Butter, Ghee, Dairy Whitener, Greek Yogurt and Curd; the year's focus was on improving capacity utilisation across all manufacturing lines to support portfolio expansion into value-added dairy. Backward integration continued on the input side, with over 60,000 litres of milk per day procured through a network of over 2,500 farmers, supported by breeding, feeding and livestock management programmes, farmer training, animal health camps, deworming drives and cattle feed distribution. Category expansion is being pursued through distribution rather than plant capex - targeted distribution expansion for differentiated rusk variants (Milk Rusk, Butter Rusk, Cake Rusk alongside the core Premium Bake Rusk portfolio), Quick commerce platform partnerships in Bread, and expanded availability across geographies. Internationally, the Company continues to evaluate opportunities to expand operations in emerging markets through contract manufacturing, partnerships and other strategic avenues, customising distribution across MENA, Americas and Asia Pacific and entering white-space markets, while pursuing automation, recipe and packaging optimisation, logistics efficiencies and sourcing optimisation. The Board's Report records no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report, and no change in the nature of the Company's business during the year. No rupee capex figure or dated commissioning schedule for a new project is disclosed in the routed sections.

risks.risk: Input cost volatility across key agri and energy commodities
risks.note: Management calls out volatility in the cost of key input items such as wheat, sugar, milk, edible oils, crude oil & gas as a key risk that may require calibrated pricing and cost management actions; elevated cocoa costs are separately flagged as pressuring Cake category profitability. Because the portfolio is commodity-intensive and price-sensitive at the ` 5/- and ` 10/- points, cost spikes cannot be fully passed through without hurting volumes.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity from regional, unorganised and digitally native players
risks.note: Competition from regional and unorganised players in value segments and emerging brands in premium segments may continue to exert pressure on pricing, profitability and market share. In Cake, low entry barriers keep the category highly fragmented; in Bread, insurgent and niche brands are investing in innovation and premium positioning; in Rusk, pricing is the key competitive differentiator in a commoditised structure.

risks.risk: Shifting consumer preferences towards health, nutrition and clean-label products
risks.note: Evolving preferences necessitate continuous portfolio adaptation and innovation; management notes that preference for healthier alternatives may affect demand for traditional offerings, requiring continuous portfolio innovation and renovation to stay relevant.

risks.risk: Execution complexity from the shift to Digital and Quick commerce channels
risks.note: Increasing reliance on Digital and Quick commerce adds execution complexity in demand planning, inventory management and channel economics, even as these channels grow faster than traditional trade and drive discovery and premiumisation.

risks.risk: Geopolitical exposure and currency volatility in international markets
risks.note: The International Business remains exposed to geopolitical developments in the Middle East and currency volatility in parts of Africa and the Levant region, leading to rising input and freight costs that may impact growth and profitability.

risks.risk: Modern Trade dominance raising the cost of operations overseas
risks.note: Modern Trade dominance in several international markets increases the cost of operations, while competition from both local and global players necessitates continued agility and focused execution.

risks.risk: Dairy-specific margin exposure - milk procurement cost, seasonality and value-added competition
risks.note: The Dairy business remains exposed to volatility in milk procurement costs which may impact margins and profitability; the value-added dairy segment faces heightened competition from organised and regional players, and demand in certain dairy categories is influenced by seasonal consumption patterns.

risks.risk: Category-development risk in early-stage and occasion-dependent categories
risks.note: Croissant remains at an early stage of development with relatively low consumer awareness, requiring sustained investment in category creation, consumer education and distribution to unlock growth; Rusk stays closely tied to tea-consumption occasions, making it important to broaden consumer appeal and expand usage occasions. The Company's cautionary statement additionally lists raw material availability and/or prices, cyclical demand, pricing, competitive actions, disruptions due to pandemic and/or natural calamities and changes in government and/or tax regulations as factors that could make a difference to operations.

one-line thesis: Britannia delivered strong 7.5% revenue and 16.3% PAT growth in FY26 despite West Asia logistics disruption and dual pricing in rural wholesale channels; margin resilience was maintained through CEP efficiency, strategic price hikes, and e-commerce premiumization, with FY27 outlook supported by normalized trade channels and accelerated D2C growth.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian economy expected to sustain strong growth momentum relative to global peers, with real GDP growth projected in the range of ~6.5 to 7%, supported by resilient domestic demand, stable financial systems and continued policy support
- Inflation expected to remain broadly within the RBI's target range, though geopolitical developments in energy markets and global supply chains may continue to influence input costs and demand conditions
- Categories supported by favourable demographic trends, increasing urbanisation, rising disposable incomes and growing preference for branded and convenient food products
- Biscuit: demand supported by favourable demographics, urbanisation, nuclear households and on-the-go lifestyles; premiumisation in urban markets and growing rural penetration provide both volume and value growth avenues
- Cake: growth potential from increasing household penetration, product innovation and premiumisation across differentiated formats such as Donuts and Brownies
- Rusk: fragmented, predominantly unorganised market structure creates an opportunity for organised players with strong brands, extensive distribution and consistent quality
- Bread: rising demand for protein-rich, high-fibre, clean-label and differentiated variants provides avenues for innovation and premiumisation, with Quick commerce enhancing access and visibility
- Dairy: adoption of Quick commerce and E-commerce is expanding consumer access, while health, wellness and convenience preferences support high-protein, nutrition-focused and ready-to-consume dairy
- Wafer: low category penetration plus growing traction in premium wafer rolls supports consumer expansion, product discovery and category development
- Croissant: increasing consumer acceptance of global bakery formats, rising disposable incomes and preference for indulgent, premium snacking as awareness expands beyond early adopters and Gen Z cohorts
- International: positioned for growth across GCC countries, Americas and Africa supported by E-commerce expansion, localised manufacturing and portfolios tailored to regional preferences, with white-space potential in Latin America, Asia, Europe and Russia
- Margin levers: calibrated pricing actions plus cost-efficiency initiatives - automation, recipe and packaging optimisation, logistics efficiencies and sourcing optimisation
- Watch-items on the demand/cost side: volatility in wheat, sugar, edible oils, crude oil & gas and cocoa; milk procurement cost volatility in Dairy; competitive intensity from regional/unorganised players in value segments and digitally native brands in premium segments
- Execution complexity is rising with increasing reliance on Digital and Quick commerce channels, in areas such as demand planning, inventory management and channel economics
- International cost headwinds from Middle East geopolitics, currency volatility in parts of Africa and the Levant, and Modern Trade dominance raising the cost of operations

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Britannia's expansion in FY 2025-26 was largely about deepening existing assets rather than building new ones. The manufacturing and supply chain network comprises 20 state-of-the-art factories supported by an integrated warehousing and distribution infrastructure, strategically located to minimise lead times and preserve product freshness; during the year the Company focused on optimising existing capacities rather than adding greenfield capacity. In Dairy, the state-of-the-art facility at Ranjangaon, Maharashtra, with a milk processing capacity of ~5 lakh litres per day, continues to anchor the multi-category dairy strategy, manufacturing Cheese, Flavoured Milk, Skimmed Milk Powder, Butter, Ghee, Dairy Whitener, Greek Yogurt and Curd; the year's focus was on improving capacity utilisation across all manufacturing lines to support portfolio expansion into value-added dairy. Backward integration continued on the input side, with over 60,000 litres of milk per day procured through a network of over 2,500 farmers, supported by breeding, feeding and livestock management programmes, farmer training, animal health camps, deworming drives and cattle feed distribution. Category expansion is being pursued through distribution rather than plant capex - targeted distribution expansion for differentiated rusk variants (Milk Rusk, Butter Rusk, Cake Rusk alongside the core Premium Bake Rusk portfolio), Quick commerce platform partnerships in Bread, and expanded availability across geographies. Internationally, the Company continues to evaluate opportunities to expand operations in emerging markets through contract manufacturing, partnerships and other strategic avenues, customising distribution across MENA, Americas and Asia Pacific and entering white-space markets, while pursuing automation, recipe and packaging optimisation, logistics efficiencies and sourcing optimisation. The Board's Report records no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report, and no change in the nature of the Company's business during the year. No rupee capex figure or dated commissioning schedule for a new project is disclosed in the routed sections.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Century-long brand franchise - the Board presented the 107th Annual Report of the Company, and the Corporate Governance Report describes 'a legacy spanning over a century'
- Extensive sales and distribution network, strengthened during the year through improved outlet servicing, enhanced rural reach and focused interventions across key geographies
- Rural reach architecture built on Rural Preferred Dealers, last-mile distribution and value-led pack-price formats at the ` 5/- and ` 10/- price points that dominate volumes
- Manufacturing scale and locational advantage - 20 state-of-the-art factories with integrated warehousing and distribution, enabling freshness and short lead times
- Innovation and premiumisation engine across biscuit, cake, dairy and adjacent categories, including India's 1st DHA-enriched biscuit 'Milk Bikis SMART' with 16 micronutrients
- Structural cost-efficiency programs across the value chain (manufacturing productivity, energy efficiency, packaging optimisation, freight and distribution rationalisation) that protect margins in a volatile cost environment
- International footprint across more than 80 countries operating largely through a national distributor-led model spanning the Middle East, Americas, Africa, Europe and Asia Pacific
- Omnichannel route-to-market spanning traditional trade for mass and rural consumption alongside Modern Trade, E-commerce and Quick commerce for premium and impulse-led purchases

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Fuel/laminate inflation persistence; delayed normalization of dual pricing in B2B channels; El Nino impact on milk supply; geopolitical disruption in Middle East; e-commerce channel conflict if INR 5/10 packs are pushed

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: E-commerce contribution is 12%+ when excluding low-price biscuits (not 6%); 70% of e-commerce sales now via quick commerce enabling premiumization; women manage majority of factories; INR 5/10 packs are deliberately deprioritized on e-commerce to avoid channel conflict; tax reversal (INR 200cr) boosted PAT by ~800bps

one-line thesis: Britannia delivered strong 7.5% revenue and 16.3% PAT growth in FY26 despite West Asia logistics disruption and dual pricing in rural wholesale channels; margin resilience was maintained through CEP efficiency, strategic price hikes, and e-commerce premiumization, with FY27 outlook supported by normalized trade channels and accelerated D2C growth.
financial scorecard: revenue: +7.5% YoY (INR 18,858cr); EBITDA/margin: +11.6% YoY, 17.0% margin (flat vs FY25); PAT (rptd): +16.3% YoY (INR 2,533cr); PAT (normalized): ~+10-12% YoY (ex-tax reversal of ~INR 200cr); order book: N/A; net debt: Net cash position maintained, no new debt raised
guidance: revenue growth: High single to low double-digit (FY27); margin: Stable to slightly pressured (fuel/laminate inflation offset by CEP); order inflow: N/A; capex/commissioning: INR 400-500cr planned (FY27), focused on automation, renewable energy, and Mundra capacity expansion
segment / subsidiary detail: Biscuits: +5.5% volume growth; Adjacencies (cake, dairy, wafers): 1.4x-3x faster than biscuits; E-commerce: 6% of total sales (12%+ when excluding INR 5/10 packs); International: impacted by Hormuz Strait disruption (Q4); Dairy: double-digit growth driven by ghee; Wafers: healthy double-digit growth
growth verticals / optionality: E-commerce premiumization (70% q-com share); Many Indias regional customization; New product launches (Cheeze Dipped, Caramel Dipped, Fudge It); Expansion of D2C offerings; Mundra export hub scaling to replace Oman
margins & cost dynamics: Wheat: deflationary trend reversed in March due to unseasonal rains; Palm oil: up 15-20% YoY but 5-month coverage; Laminate: up 10-15% post-March due to Middle East war; Fuel (LPG/CNG): significant inflation; Sugar: stable; Cost savings: CEP program delivered 10x improvement since 2013-14, doubled since 2021
capex / expansion: INR 400-500cr planned for FY27; focus: automation, renewable energy (targeting 20%+ share), packaging optimization, Mundra export unit expansion
capital allocation: Prioritizing CEP efficiency, brand marketing (ad spend up), e-commerce investments, and capex for resilience; no dividend cut; buybacks not mentioned

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

hero.oneLiner: Britannia Industries is a century-old Indian packaged-foods company operating in a single 'Foods' segment, spanning bakery (biscuit, cake, rusk, bread), dairy and adjacent snacking categories in India and in more than 80 export markets.
